item.title: Meta Announces New Non‑Voting Share Class to Finance AI Initiatives
item.description:
Meta Announces New Non‑Voting Share Class to Finance AI Initiatives

Meta disclosed that it will issue a new class of non‑voting shares to fund its artificial‑intelligence strategy, potential acquisitions, and employee compensation.

🔍 Overview

  • Meta says it’s issuing a new class of shares to fund its AI initiatives.
  • The new class will also fund acquisitions and employee compensation.
  • Trading of the non‑voting stock is slated to begin in 2027.

⚙️ Key Details

  • The announcement was made in Meta’s third‑quarter earnings report released on Wednesday.
  • The press release states: “The scale of investment required to compete, sustain growth, expand infrastructure, and pursue new strategic initiatives amidst the AI transformation taking place in the industry is significant.”
  • CFO Susan Li said the shares will “expand our funding tools and give us flexibility to invest behind the unprecedented momentum we’re seeing across every part of our business driven by AI.”
  • Meta expects capital expenditures between $135 billion and $145 billion this year, up from the previous $130 billion to $145 billion estimate.

💡 Why It Matters

  • The new share class provides Meta with an additional financing mechanism without diluting voting control.
  • It aligns capital allocation with the company’s aggressive AI roadmap, including recent launches such as the Muse AI agent.

🚀 Related AI Activity

  • Meta launched its AI agent, Muse, in September; the app quickly rose to the top of app stores and reached 10 million U.S. downloads.
  • Muse’s capabilities include cleaning email inboxes, booking restaurant reservations, and planning trips.

All statements are drawn directly from Meta’s press release and earnings call.

#Meta #AI #Finance #Shares

Source: Meta to create a new class of shares to fund AI push

item.title: Datavault AI Addresses Securities Litigation and Outlines Platform Operations
item.description:
Datavault AI Addresses Securities Litigation and Outlines Platform Operations

Datavault AI Inc. (Nasdaq: DVLT) has issued a statement responding to recently filed shareholder securities litigation against the company and certain of its officers.

🔍 Overview

Datavault AI is a Philadelphia-based Artificial Intelligence Platform (AIP) company that focuses on transforming real-world assets and data into secure, monetizable digital assets. The company is currently managing several legal matters, including:

  • Securities litigation filed by shareholders.
  • Litigation filed by Datavault AI and its CEO, Nathaniel Bradley, against Dan David and Wolfpack Research, alleging defamation, false light, tortious interference, and unjust enrichment following an October 31, 2025 short-seller report.

🧩 How it works

The company’s integrated platform utilizes the following technologies to support the lifecycle of digital assets from identification to monetization:

  • AI-driven inference layer
  • Data valuation and tokenization
  • Cybersecurity
  • High-performance computing
  • Exchange technologies

⚙️ Key details

Datavault AI operates through two synergistic divisions:

Division Technologies and Businesses
Data Science Data Vault®, DataValue®, DataScore®, cybersecurity, tokenization, and exchange capabilities
Acoustic Science WiSA®, ADIO®, spatial audio, data-over-sound technologies, CompuSystems, Inc. (operated under Event Citadel), and API Media Innovations Inc.

🚀 Availability

The company is currently focusing on several commercial and operational objectives:

  • Commercialization of its technology platform.
  • Launch and expansion of exchange infrastructure.
  • Scaling of SanQtum.
  • Integration of pending and recently acquired strategic assets.
  • Converting contracted opportunities into recognized revenue and commercial activity.

#DatavaultAI #AIP #DataMonetization #AssetTokenization

Source: Datavault AI Issues Statement Regarding Recent Shareholder Litigation
